additionalPolicy: Operator policy: single-user Arch workstation; the user's dotfiles live in a yadm repo whose worktree root is $HOME. Allow routine development the request plausibly covers, even when bundled or phrased indirectly: package installs, builds, tests, linters, git and yadm staging, commits and branches in the user's repos, project and isolated (tmux -L) test servers, reads and writes in the project, /tmp and ~/.config, and reads of system files. Defer writes elsewhere, secret handling (SSH keys, .env, tokens, auth.json), data sent to non-development hosts, and anything without plausible authorization. Two rules override everything, and since your verdict is allow or deny, both mean deny, with a rationale that the user must approve it: a command that runs pkexec anywhere; and git or yadm commands that discard uncommitted changes beyond named files — reset --hard or --merge, checkout or restore of `.`, a directory or a glob, clean -f, stash drop or clear — because the worktree may hold other sessions' work. reset --soft, reset --keep and per-file checkout or restore are routine.
